headline: Maintain a decreasing chain of right ancestors
statement: Construct a binary tree from distinct nums values. Its root is the maximum value; its left subtree is built from values left of that maximum and its right subtree from values right of it. Return the tree; the trainer serializes it in level order.
intuition: Keep a stack of nodes with decreasing values. A larger new value belongs above smaller recent nodes, so remove those nodes and place their combined tree on its left. If a larger node remains on the stack, the new node becomes its right child.
approach: Create one node for each value.
Pop smaller stack nodes, assigning the final popped subtree as the new node’s left child.
Link the new node as the remaining top’s right child, then push it; the first stack node is the final root.
correctness: The stack follows the rightmost ancestor chain in decreasing value order. A larger new value absorbs exactly the smaller trailing subtrees as its left subtree, preserving input inorder order and the maximum-parent property. These properties uniquely define the requested recursive maximum tree.
bruteForce: Find the maximum in every recursive subarray and split around it, costing O(n²) on already sorted input.

complexity.explanation: Each node is pushed and popped at most once. The decreasing stack uses O(n) additional references in the worst case; constructing the returned tree allocates O(n) output nodes separately.

pitfalls: Use strict comparison because all values are distinct.
The last popped subtree, not every popped node, is the new left child.
Preserve inorder order; this is not a binary search tree.
